architecture.mechanism: Infrared-based sensing to detect changes in tubing content (air vs. fluid) coupled with automatic mechanical occlusion actuation.
architecture.intervention: Retrofit an infrared emitter-detector pair around the existing disposable tubing downstream of the pump cassette to monitor refractive index changes indicative of flow stagnation or micro-bubble accumulation preceding total occlusion, triggering a pinch-valve actuator before pressure thresholds are reached.
architecture.expected_effect: Detection of flow cessation or impedance changes up to ten minutes prior to traditional pressure-based alarm activation while maintaining the integrity of the disposable flow path and reducing false alarms caused by transient pressure spikes.
architecture.falsification_test: Induce a controlled downstream occlusion in a test rig with varying fluid viscosities and measure the time delta between the infrared sensor's trigger signal and the standard pump pressure alarm; failure occurs if the delta is less than ten minutes or if false triggers exceed 1% during simulated patient movement.
